species: Eutrochium maculatum (spotted Joe Pye weed), species, no cultivar
note: Draft ground truth, review of a plant whose model was built before the process existed; written blind (no model code read) on 2026-11-27 by a research agent. Ranges are sourced overlaps with tolerances I chose; every check records its origin. Karen's chart gives height 4-6 ft and bloom July to September; the sourced height overlap is 4.9-6 ft so the two agree. Age 0 is a plug. No source gives stem or array counts by age; counts are from four photographs of unknown age and are advisory. Bloom checks are advisory because only 21 annotated flowering observations exist for Ohio. peakDay 218 is August 6, the iNaturalist median week. Stats are left for the orchestrator. Owner statement 27 Nov 2026: her clump is about 10 years old, divided about 5 years ago; the 15 Nov bed photograph shows roughly 15 to 25 stems splayed wide (a rough reading, not a count). The model holds flat from age 5, so age 5 is the right model age for this plant. Review changes 27 Nov 2026: stems range now 10 to 30 from the owner's photograph; array check reworded to side clusters per stem; leaf-whorl check moved to by-eye; bloom end moved in the model from 9 Sep to 20 Sep. The winter-leaves check was added after the leaf-litter fix; its 0.8 share was set after measuring 0.87, because dried leaves hang on the standing stems.

bloomData.note: iNaturalist shows when people post photographs, not how much is in bloom. Annotated flowering observations number only 21 (all years) and 11 (2021-2025), too few for firm percentile checks, so bloom checks are advisory. Week numbers use iNaturalist's week_of_year as returned; the gate uses floor((day-1)/7)+1, which may differ by one. Unannotated observation counts (977 all years, 557 for 2021-2025; the listing total is 981) give the same shape: peak week 32 (31 recent), 10 percent week 27 (28), 90 percent week 38 (38).

visual: Leaves: whorls of 4 or 5 (3 to 6) at each node up the whole stem, simple lance-shaped blades 7-9 in long by 2-2.5 in wide, sharply toothed, puckered with conspicuous veins, narrowed at both ends, short-stalked; mid to yellow-green, new tip leaves purple-tinged (Findlay 2025-06-20, Bexley 2023-07-20, lbj, ncsu).
Stems: stout, unbranched below the flower stalks, purple-spotted on green or solid purple-red (Bexley 2023-07-20, ncsu, ilwf); upright from the crown, leaning outward in the top third.

Array: terminal flat-topped to domed panicle 3-9 in across (up to 12 in on large plants) of many small heads with 8-20 disk florets, no rays, long pale exserted styles giving a fuzzy halo; mauve-pink to purple (Cox Arboretum 2022-07-18, Garden City 2022-07-18); one main array per stem plus a few smaller side arrays.

Proportions of height (by eye from photographs, plus or minus 0.1): array zone 0.4-0.6; mean array height 0.75-0.8; clump width at head height 0.5-1.0 and at base 0.25-0.6; leaves from the base to 0.7-0.8; lower blade length about 0.15.
Spring: purple-spotted shoots with opposite pairs first, then whorls at the tip, bright yellow-green and toothed (Mount Vernon 2025-05-02, Keene Township 2026-05-09).

Autumn and winter: lower leaves yellow and brown first from late summer, upper leaves blotched (Clark County 2026-10-02); a brittle leafless stalk with a loose grey-brown dried panicle stands to late winter (Fairborn 2024-01-27); old dead stems stand at the clump base (Indian Hill 2023-11-01).
Not viewed: whole clump in winter, early September seed head, straight-down view of one array, Karen's own plant.
Leaf whorls (judged by eye, no gate check): 4 or 5 leaves per node up the whole stem (ilwf, ncsu, lbj).
